note: Artwork registered 2026-09-30 during Ingram's /goal (create and register Episode 1 art). Place art follows the scene/location template (no people, 1990s Japanese animation background art, matte painting with gouache and watercolour texture, --ar 2:1, stylize 200, subtle upscale once). The visual language: teal-grey is the cold, stone-cut authority of institutions; warm orange golden-hour light is the life inside them.

registrations.note: Ward Four at night for the General Hospital haunt: two rows of iron beds under small blue night lamps, an old brass sign over the door, and one warm amber lamp at the night desk at the far end. The whole room is cold institutional teal; the only life in it is that one lamp, which is the night sister. Picked from the third frame of the first batch (the centred lamp and the sign over the door read best), then subtle-upscaled.

The Crew Mess: the bar made from a sheet of Frame armour plate across two oil drums, the huge chalk slate of crews and tabs behind it, wet coats hung on hooks, three orange lamps in teal machine-shop shadow. Teal is the dock's steel; orange is the crews' warmth. Second frame of the batch, subtle-upscaled.

The Bathhouse: the big tiled pool under a painted harbour mural, slanting pale-gold afternoon light through tall windows, steam, wooden lockers and the attendant's high seat. The first attempt used 'warm orange light streaming through high windows into steam' and the windows read as a building on fire, so it was redone gentler (pale gold, calm and peaceful). Fourth frame of the second batch, subtle-upscaled.

Row C, Block 3, the overflow block for An Early Night: a long plywood corridor under a tin roof, packing crates for nightstands, one iron radiator, and at the far end a single doorway glowing orange where the warden's lamp is on. Teal is the building; the orange doorway is the one person awake looking after them. The other frame with a figure in the doorway was rejected (scene art has no people). Subtle-upscaled.

The Shrine Gate at dusk: a faded red torii, the fat straw rope hung with paper fortunes, the stone basin, the offering box with a cat on top, one paper lantern glowing orange against a teal-grey street. The one warm thing on the block. Second frame of the batch, subtle-upscaled.

The Roof of Row E, Block 9: a flat tarred roof with a low wall, the water tank on iron legs, the ladder top and a blanket, and across the black harbour the whole of Kurose lit gold and orange up its hills under a deep teal sky. The clearest single picture of the contrast this campaign wants: a cold sky, a warm city. Top-left frame, subtle-upscaled.

The Rumour Mill: Row B, Block 8's common room after lights out, a blanket pinned over the window, one lamp on the floor throwing orange up the wall, the kettle on its hot plate, the armchair with the fat notebook left on it, dressing gowns on the hooks. Second frame, subtle-upscaled.

The Night Observer: the Met Office roof, the white slatted instrument box, the copper rain bucket, the mast with its spinning cups, the barometer and the chalkboard by the door, one orange lamp above the stair head, and the black harbour with a far shore of small lights. Fourth frame, subtle-upscaled.

The Night Shift: No. 1 Machine Shop, tall as a church, two gantry cranes under the roof, pools of hard white lamplight with darkness between, and the huge lower leg of a Frame standing in its pit, with a few warm orange sparks at the right. Third frame, subtle-upscaled.

The Market Hall after hours, for the Magic Show: shuttered stalls against the walls, rows of borrowed benches, blankets pinned over the high windows, and at the back a scaffold holding the Oddwater Company's lantern with its orange light. A cold hall with one warm thing waiting to happen. Second frame, subtle-upscaled.

The Card Game: Row F, Block 5's common room, the round table under its one good hanging lamp with mismatched chairs, the ginger cat on the radiator, the door-sized chalk debt board on the wall, damp coats on hooks, and one pool of orange light on the boards under the table. Second frame, subtle-upscaled.
